newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Details of EU, Boeing agreement on merger.
newsitem.headline: Details of EU, Boeing agreement on merger.

text.p: Following is a list of the concessions made by Boeing Co. to win European Union regulatory approval for its $15 billion acquisition of McDonnell Douglas Corp.
The list is based on a written statement by Boeing and comments made by European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert at a news conference.
-- BOEING'S EXCLUSIVE SUPPLY PACTS WITH AIRLINES

Boeing agreed not to conclude any new exclusive aircraft supply contracts with airlines before Aug. 1, 2007. It also agreed not to enforce the exclusivity provisions in its existing contracts with AMR Corp.'s American Airlines, Continental Airlines Inc. and Delta Air Lines Inc.

Boeing agreed to license any patents and know-how obtained under U.S. government-financed contracts or research and development programmes if used in Boeing's commercial aviation business. Van Miert said there would be an arbitration procedure to solve any conflicts.
Boeing agreed to license patents to other commercial aircraft manufacturers "on a non-exclusive, reasonable-royalty basis."

McDonnell Douglas's commercial aircraft operations will be kept in a separate legal entity within the merged company for 10 years. Van Miert said he had considered asking Boeing to sell Douglas Aircraft, McDonnell Douglas' commercial aviation division, but had found there were no potential buyers.

Van Miert added that while airlines had privately expressed concerns about the merger, "a majority was not in favour of cutting off the servicing (of Douglas planes) and (manufacturing) of spare parts and we took that into account."
Van Miert said the commission also received commitments from Boeing that it would not abuse its position vis-a-vis current McDonnell airline customers.

Boeing said it intended to provide customer support for existing McDonnell Douglas commercial aircraft "at the same high-quality level provided for Boeing aircraft." But it also agreed not to use such customer support as leverage to obtain any advantage in sales of new commercial airacraft.
-- NO EXCLUSIVE CONTRACTS BETWEEN BOEING AND ITS SUPPLIERS
Van Miert said Boeing would not abuse its position with its suppliers and that it would refrain from signing any exclusive contracts with them.
Boeing said it agreed not to interfere unduly with actual or potential relationships between its suppliers and other commercial aircraft manufacturers.
